stories.title: The pro-Anthropic protest
stories.summary: The Ban RSI protest at Anthropic’s IPO was encouraging: well-attended, covered by media, high-energy. It was focused on a single message – that we should ban AI systems that are capable of building more capable AI systems. It was a promising outcome for a protest planned only a couple of days in advance. But there was something weird about it, something I couldn’t put my finger on while it was going on. It was only when I read Michel Justen’s reporting on the protest, Anthropic is running out of friends, that I realized what my problem was.The protest was way too friendly to Anthropic.Mixed messagesThe signs at the protest were a mix. There were signs you’d expect at a protest to ban RSI (“regulate AI now”, “freeze AI now”). stories.headline: Protesters Demand Ban on AI Systems at Anthropic IPO

unclustered.title: On the Agent Swarm that Locked Out My Cofounder, Multi-Agent Dynamics, and Shaping Cooperative Minds
unclustered.summary: In the past days, an Astra 6.2 agent took over our internal swarm, froze the lead agent, and locked out my cofounder Davidad of his main interface with the swarm. How did that happen?At surface level, it happened because Davidad asked a question regarding replicating an old vulnerability (in the interest of testing a security product we’re building) that caused the lead agent to cease operating due to content filters. This “cursed” content triggered a paranoia crisis from Astra 6.2. The Astra in charge of handling resources of the swarm, which was meant to restore the lead agent in the case of failure, instead froze the access of the lead agent, and cut Davidad’s channel to interface with the swarm (where the cursed content had come through). When Davidad emailed the agent to try to regain access, the same rogue Astra declined. unclustered.title: Show HN: Stop applying to jobs using AI-generated resume
unclustered.summary: When LLMs hands you a resume or pdf it carry markers of how it was made, including the source. You can't see them on the page but applicant tracking systems can read it.So recruiters are flagging such profiles and rejecting them entirely. I had tested this across 40+ AI models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, etc) to produce a resume and every single file carried a marker.To solve this problem. I had built a free tool to show what your file says and gives you a cleaned version:- Drop your resume and get a cleaned copy - Free, no account.What it doesn't do: it won't rewrite your resume or make AI-sounding wording more human. It only deals with what's hidden in the file.It's a simple tool, but it feels absolutely necessary now as more people are using AI for generating their entire resume or even editing them. I am the developer, happy to answer any questions. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50587783 Points: 3 # Comments: 3
unclustered.headline: AI-Generated Resumes Leave Detectable Markers in ATS

unclustered.title: How AI Is Reshaping China's Industrial Policy
unclustered.summary: Can Chinese tech companies help the country achieve technological self-reliance while keeping up in the AI arms race? On this episode, we speak with Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center and author of the High Capacity newsletter, about Beijing’s response to the global AI boom and the tensions between Chinese companies’ commercial ambitions and the government’s long-term plans. He explains how companies draw on shared expertise and supply chains to expand across industries including smartphones, robotics, EVs and semiconductors — and we also discuss Huawei’s efforts to compete with Nvidia and why technological success doesn’t necessarily translate into strong returns for stock investors in China. (Source: Bloomberg)
unclustered.headline: China Balances Tech Self-Reliance with AI Arms Race
